item.title: About
item.description: Nano Tank ATO Reliability is a small content site focused on one thing: helping aquarium hobbyists avoid dumb, expensive, or stressful auto-top-off mistakes in nano and open-top tanks. The site is built around practical guidance, including: troubleshooting repeated overfill behavior understanding common failure modes comparing sensor and system tradeoffs thinking more carefully about reservoir size, maintenance burden, and real-world setup risk This is not meant to be a hype machine.

item.title: ATO Maintenance Schedule for Nano Tanks
item.description: Why maintenance matters here ATO systems usually do not leap straight from “fine” to “catastrophe.” They drift there through dirt, salt creep, movement, neglected tubing, and warning behavior that gets normalized because it seemed minor the first few times. item.description: Why false alarms are not harmless False ATO alarms are annoying, but the bigger problem is what they train you to do. item.title: Float Switch vs Optical Sensor ATOs for Nano Tanks
item.description: The real question The useful question is not which sensor sounds more advanced on a product page. The useful question is how each sensing approach behaves when the tank gets dirty, the mount shifts slightly, or maintenance gets delayed because life is annoying. In nano tanks, tiny errors matter faster. That makes graceful failure more important than gadget marketing. Short answer Float switches are mechanically simple and easy to understand, but they can stick, drag, or get obstructed.
